According to the EU Electricity Balancing Guideline, each European transmission system operator should use the single imbalance pricing method which treats both deviation directions the same, no matter if a deviation helps the system or pushes it away from the balance. This paper aims to investigate the behavior of a hybrid facility consisting of an uncontrollable RES, a battery and an electrolyzer under such market setting. The formulated mathematical model of the hybrid facility seeks to maximize profit in the day-ahead energy market, while minimizing the imbalance costs. Uncertainty of the RES output is captured using stochastic scenarios, while the direction of the power system deviation, relevant for the imbalance pricing, is modeled using a newly proposed robust approach. Results of the case study indicate that the single imbalance pricing scheme might bring flexible assets to temptation of intentional deviations should they anticipate favorable imbalance prices.

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of distributed synchronous condensers considering voltage support capability enhancement in HVDC sending-end AC power system
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative optimal allocation method for distributed synchronous condensers (DSCs) in the high voltage direct current (HVDC) sending-end AC power system, designed to significantly enhance the system voltage support capability and effectively suppress the overvoltage issues. With the increasing integration of large-scale renewable energy sources (RESs) into the HVDC sending-end AC power system, the system short-circuit ratio and voltage support capability are compromised, which may easily cause the prominent overvoltage problem after the HVDC fault. Our method addresses these challenges by not only enhancing the system voltage support capability but also suppressing the overvoltage problems. The impact of DSCs on multiple renewable energy stations short circuit ratio (MRSCR) of the system is analyzed, and a comprehensive quantitative evaluation index of voltage support capability that can quantitatively represent the system voltage support capability enhancement after installing DSCs is defined. A multi-objective optimization model for DSCs allocation is proposed with the objectives of simultaneously minimizing the investment cost and maximizing the system voltage support capability enhancement. The optimal installation positions and configuration quantities (capacities) of DSCs are then obtained by solving the optimization model. Simulation studies conducted on a practical power system demonstrate the method's effectiveness in maximizing system voltage support capability enhancement, suppressing overvoltage issues, and offering superior economic performance compared to the centralized synchronous condensers (CSCs) configuration method.

articleTitle: High-quality sample generation for power system transient stability assessment based on data-driven methods
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Deep learning technology is identified as a valid tool for transient stability assessment (TSA). Moreover, the superior performance of TSA model depends on generous labeled samples. However, power grid is a dynamic system, and there are some topologies or operation conditions changes substantially. The traditional manner is to generate a great quantity of samples for each specific topology. Nonetheless, it is very time-consuming to generate these labeled samples and establish TSA models. In order to build a high-quality offline samples database for TSA model training and updating, this paper proposes a high-quality sample generation framework based on data-driven methods. Firstly, the representative topologies provided by system operator are clustered into four different categories by density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN), thus the corresponding samples are collected. Then, when a new topology is encountered in the online application, the principle of scenario matching is used to match the most similar topology category. After that, the instance-based transfer learning is implemented from database of the best matched topology category. Finally, deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) is constructed to mitigate the class-imbalance problem, that is, unstable scenarios occur far rarely than the stable scenarios. Consequently, a high-quality and balanced database for TSA model training and updating is constructed. The comprehensive test results on the Central China Power Grid illustrate that the proposed framework can generate high-quality and balanced TSA samples. Furthermore, the samples generation time is dramatically shortened. In addition, the metrics of accuracy, reliability and adaptability of TSA model are significantly enhanced.

articleTitle: On degeneracy issues in multi-parametric programming and critical region exploration based distributed optimization in smart grid operations
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Improving renewable energy resource utilization efficiency is crucial to reducing carbon emissions, and multiparametric programming has provided a systematic perspective in conducting analysis and optimization toward this goal in smart grid operations. This paper focuses on two aspects of interest related to multi-parametric linear/quadratic programming (mpLP/QP). First, we study degeneracy issues of mpLP/QP. A novel approach to deal with degeneracies is proposed to find all critical regions containing the given parameter. Our method leverages properties of the multi-parametric linear complementary problem, vertex searching technique, and complementary basis enumeration. In this way, the essence of degeneracy is reflected by the nonuniqueness of the complementary basis. Finding such bases proves helpful in generating related critical regions. Second, an improved critical region exploration (CRE) method to solve distributed LP/QP is proposed under a general mpLP/QP-based formulation. The improved CRE incorporates the proposed approach to handle degeneracies. A cutting plane update and an adaptive stepsize scheme are also integrated to accelerate convergence under different problem settings. The computational efficiency is verified on multi-area tie-line scheduling problems with various testing benchmarks and initial states.

articleTitle: Digital twin-supported battery state estimation based on TCN-LSTM neural networks and transfer learning
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Estimating battery states such as State of Charge (SOC) and State of Health (SOH) is an essential component in developing energy storage technologies, which require accurate estimation of complex and nonlinear systems. A significant challenge is extracting pertinent spatial and temporal features from original battery data, which is crucial for efficient battery management systems. The emergence of digital twin (DT) technology offers a novel opportunity for performance monitoring and management of lithium-ion batteries, enhancing collaborative capacity among different battery state estimation techniques and enabling optimal operation of battery storage units. In this study, we propose a DT-supported battery state estimation method, in collaboration with the temporal convolutional network (TCN) and the long short-term memory (LSTM), to address the challenge of feature extraction. Firstly, we introduce a 4-layer hierarchical DT to overcome computational and data storage limitations in conventional battery management systems. Secondly, we present an online algorithm, TCN-LSTM for battery state estimation. Compared to conventional methods, TCN-LSTM outperforms other cyclic networks in various sequence modelling tasks and exhibits reduced reliance on the initial state conditions of the battery. Our methodology employs transfer learning to dynamically adjust the neural network parameters based on fresh data, ensuring real-time updating and enhancing the DT's accuracy. Focusing on SOC, SOH and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation, our model demonstrates exceptional results. When testing with 90 cycle data, the average root mean square error (RMSE) values for SOC, SOH, and RUL are 1.1 %, 0.8%, and 0.9 % respectively, significantly outperforming traditional CNN's 2.2%, 2.0% and 3.6% and others. These results un-equivocally demonstrate the contribution of the DT model to battery management, highlighting the outstanding robustness of our proposed method, showcasing consistent performance across various conditions and superior adaptability compared to other models.

articleTitle: Data-driven subsynchronous oscillation suppression for renewable energy integrated power systems based on Koopman operator
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Recently, subsynchronous oscillations (SSOs) have emerged frequently worldwide, with the high penetration of renewable power generation in modern power systems. The SSO introduced by renewables has become a prominent new stability problem, seriously threatening the stable operation of systems. This paper proposes a data-driven dynamic optimal controller for renewable energy integrated power systems, to suppress SSOs with the control of renewables. The challenges of the controller design are the nonlinearity, complexity and hard accessibility of the system models. Using Koopman operator, the system dynamics are accurately extracted from data and utilized to the linear model predictive control (MPC). Firstly, the globally linear representation of the system dynamics is obtained by lifting, and the key states are selected as control signals by analyzing Koopman participation factors. Subsequently, augmented with control terms, the Koopman linear parameter-varying predictor of the nonlinear controlled system is constructed, acting as a more accurate predictor. Finally, using the computationally efficient linear MPC within the lifted Koopman space, the proposed controller computes control signals online in a moving horizon fashion. Case studies show that the proposed fully data-driven SSO suppression controller is effective, adaptive and robust in various conditions, surpassing other controllers with reliable control performance.

articleTitle: PMU-based online real-time linear power flow calculation method with minimizing probability errors
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: With large-scale access to renewable energy, long-distance transmission via hybrid AC-DC networks and frequent load fluctuations, measurement-based online power flow calculation needs to be adapted to the volatility and randomness of modern power systems, and the high accuracy and real-time performance are required for online power flow. However, the traditional power flow method suffers from long calculation times, the convergence difficulty and the inaccuracy caused by RTU asynchronous errors. Therefore, a PMU-based online accurate linear power flow method with minimizing the probability errors of power flow is proposed to improve the accuracy and real-time performance. This power flow method no longer bounds PQ, PV or V0 buses, and establishes a linear relationship between the voltage measurements and the current measurements. To address the problems of complicated PMU measurement errors and the high proportion of low-quality data, a 0–1 integer programming model is established to select a set of linear measurement equations for minimizing probability errors, and a complete method of PMU-based linear power flow calculation is proposed. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed linear power flow calculation method is verified on IEEE 39 bus system and a large-scale power grid in China.

articleTitle: Energy management platform for large-scale heterogeneous energy systems: Design, implementation and application
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The unified dispatching and integrated management of heterogeneous energy systems are the keys to fully utilizing the complementary advantages of multiple energy sources. Data from such energy management platforms can contribute to the digital transformation of multienergy systems to realize data services and added business value. In this paper, in accordance with the characteristics and operational requirements of the heterogeneous energy system in the Guangzhou Higher Education Mega Center, a flexible, universal, and intelligent energy management platform is designed as a cloud base. This platform integrates intelligent electronic devices, cloud components, PaaS parallel stream computing, and cloud-edge collaborative technology. The proposed platform has the functions of supervisory control, intelligent interaction, optimization and decision-making, and other energy management services, through which it can improve the coordinated and optimized operation capacity and energy utilization rate of the heterogeneous energy system in the Guangzhou Higher Education Mega Center. The proposed design scheme can be used as a reference for constructing an integrated management platform for heterogeneous urban energy systems.

articleTitle: An extended nonlinear stability assessment methodology for type-4 wind turbines via time reversal trajectory
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: As the integration of renewable energy generation increases and as conventional generation is phased out, there is a gradual decline in the grid's strength and resilience at the connection point of wind turbines (WTs). Previous studies have shown that traditional grid-following controlled converters exhibit deteriorating dynamic characteristics and may result in an unstable system when connected to a weak grid. Due to the limitations of linear analysis, transient stability investigations are necessary. However, existing methods, such as standalone timedomain simulations or analytical Lyapunov stability criteria, have drawbacks, including computational intensity or excessive conservatism. Our prior research proposed an innovative approach to estimate the system boundary — a time-limited region of attraction (TLRoA), using a hybrid linearised Lyapunov function-based method and the time-reversal technique to compensate for the known limitations. However, in that work, the accuracy of the estimated TLRoA was not investigated, i.e. the TLRoA was not compared against a forward simulated region of attraction, and the sensitivity of the system parameters on the TLRoA was not explored. Moreover, the framework did not consider nonlinear control elements such as PLL saturation. In this paper, we not only build upon our previous work and propose directions that address these gaps but also enhance its effectiveness by introducing optimal sampling to improve further the speed of estimating the TLRoA. Furthermore, the stability boundary is verified using time-domain simulation studies in PSCAD.

articleTitle: Hierarchical and distributed control of AC and DC microgrid clusters interconnected by flexible DC distribution network
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical and distributed control method for AC and DC microgrid clusters interconnected by the flexible DC distribution network to simultaneously achieve multiple control objectives. A hierarchical and distributed control framework is firstly established, which includes the distributed generator layer (DG-layer), microgrid layer (MG-layer), and cluster coordination layer (CC-layer) to realize the decomposition of control functions. Subsequently, the control method of each layer is provided. Two control modes, i.e., the distributed master-slave control mode and distributed peer-to-peer control mode, are proposed to adapt to different control requirements for the voltages of the DC distribution network. The proposed control method can also achieve the coordination among the interlinking converters of each MG. Finally, time-domain simulations in MATLAB/Simulink platform are performed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Fault current coefficient based single-ended protection for DC collection system of offshore wind farms
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Offshore wind DC collection systems (DCCS) offer significant advantages over AC collection systems, including high transmission efficiency and small converter size. When a high-resistance fault occurs in the collection line, the traditional DC protections that rely on transient currents may face rejections and prone to false activations due to measurement noise. To address those problems, this paper proposes a single-ended protection based on nonlinear approximation of fault current coefficient (FCC). First, the fault evolution characteristics of the DCCS are analyzed, revealing that the FCC has a weak correlation with fault transition resistance and differences exist between internal and external faults. The FCCs are then extracted using the Bayesian-Trust Region-Levenberg Marquardt (B-TR-LM) method applied to the overall window data. Additionally, the FCCs are utilized to establish criteria and employed for fault identification. The proposed method is validated through application to a detailed offshore wind DCCS in Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS). Hardware-in-the-loop simulation results validate that the method can precisely detect all types of faults within 3 ms, and it enhances the transition resistance handling from 30 Ω to 50 Ω and improves noise immunity from 30 dB to 20 dB.

articleTitle: Feasibility analysis and design of a novel gas-electricity integrated transmission system
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: An increasing number of large-scale renewable plants are generating abundant electricity. As power-to-gas and power-to-x technologies become promising ways to utilize surplus electricity to enhance the flexibility of energy systems, an innovative gas-electricity integrated transmission system (GEITS) to co-transmit electricity and hydrogen or other gas products is proposed, with the foreseeable advantages of compact structure, lower installation cost, and larger energy capacity. This paper investigates the feasibility of GEITS, suggests a design guideline, and gives the operation technical parameters of GEITS in different application scenarios. The dimensions and operating pressures of GEITS benchmark natural gas pipelines and then the nominal voltages of GEITS are calculated based on the electrical strength of high-pressure hydrogen. The nominal ampacities of GEITS are evaluated by temperature-rising simulations, which are larger than those of other transmission lines. Furthermore, high-pressure flowing hydrogen acting as an electrical insulator is a novel topic, and it is investigated via experimental validation on a scale model. Although the effect of 0.4 m/s flowing hydrogen on discharge characteristics has not been observed compared to static hydrogen, the discharge is impaired in 2.4 m/s flowing nitrogen. Future works will investigate the electrical strength of high-pressure long-distance hydrogen gaps under lightning impulse tests and the discharge phenomenon in higher flowing-velocity hydrogen. Methane and methane blended with hydrogen with higher insulation performance can increase the nominal voltages.

articleTitle: Achieving an Accurate Random Process Model for PV Power Using Cheap Data: Leveraging the SDE and Public Weather Reports
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Stochastic differential equation (SDE)-based random process models of renewable energy sources (RESs) jointly capture evolving probability distribution and temporal correlation in continuous time. It enabled recent studies to remarkably improve performance of power system dynamic uncertainty quantification and optimization. However, considering the non-homogeneous random process nature of PV, there still remains a challenging question: how can a realistic and accurate daily SDE model for PV power be obtained that reflects its weather-dependent and non-Gaussian uncertainty in operation, especially when high-resolution numerical weather prediction (NWP) or sky imager is unavailable for many distributed plants? To fill this gap, this article finds that an accurate SDE model for PV power can be constructed only using the data from low-resolution public weather reports. Specifically, for each day, an hourly parameterized Jacobi diffusion process recreates temporal patterns of PV volatility. Its parameters are mapped from the day's public weather reports to reflect varying weather conditions using a simple learning model. The SDE model jointly captures intraday and intrahour volatility. Statistical examination shows that the proposed approach outperforms a selection of the latest deep learning-based time series models on real-world data collected in Macau.

articleTitle: An electromechanical joint analytic method for switching procedure of vacuum on-load tap changer in UHV converter transformer
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: As one of the key components of UHV converter transformer, the suitable switching condition of vacuum on-load tap changer (OLTC) is essential for the stability of power system. It is extremely desirable to interpret OLTC's switching procedure to assess OLTC's switching condition. However, such work can't be solved by vibration analysis alone. Therefore, an innovative electromechanical comprehensive analysis method is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a joint motor drive current, vibration and electromagnetic signals online monitoring system is established, and deployed in a VRG type OLTC in ±800kV converter station. Secondly, independent component analysis (ICA), dynamic time warping (DTW) and wavelet transform (WT) are used for processing of motor current, UHFCT and vibration signals, respectively, to extract electromechanical pulses corresponding to OLTC's contact actions. Thirdly, the switching procedure of OLTC is revealed by comprehensively analyzing the corresponding time relationship between these extracted pulses, combined with OLTC's timing sequence. The methodologies developed in this paper can help to interpret OLTC's switching procedure for deeper and finer online condition assessment.

articleTitle: Estimating Transient Stability Regions of Large-Scale Power Systems Part II: Reduced-Order Stability Region with Computational Efficiency
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Part II of this paper presents a reduced-order stability region (ROSR) based method to estimate the full-order stability region (FOSR) of a large-scale power system. First, we introduce the definitions of FOSR and ROSR, followed by a comprehensive theory that reveals the relationships between them. Since the full-order system can be rewritten as a standard two timescale model and the reduced-order system is regarded as the slow subsystem of it, the proposed theory is derived based on the idea of singular perturbation. With rigorous mathematical proof, the properties of FOSR and ROSR are revealed. Moreover, a modified Energy Augmented Dynamic (EAD) algorithm and a constrained equidistant projection (CEP) approach are employed to estimate the ROSR and FOSR, respectively. The modified EAD algorithm and CEP form a so-called reduced-order stability region mapping (ROSRM) method. Finally, the proposed ROSRM method is applied to the IEEE 10-machine-39-bus power system, and simulation studies confirm its superiority to the traditional energy function method in terms of computational speed and reliability of results.

articleTitle: Breakdown modeling of HVAC-GIL tri-post insulator subjected to electric field and mechanical loading
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: This research develops a simulation model, aiming to study the breakdown process of the tri-post insulator when exposed to electric field and mechanical loadings. The insulator is subjected to external forces of varying magnitudes and directions, along with an applied 1100 kV AC voltage. Results show that the breakdown process is driven by the electrostatic energy density (W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ele</inf>) under an AC voltage. As the length of the breakdown channel increases, W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ele</inf>, also rises, thereby accelerating the extension of the breakdown channel. After applying a straight tension along the insulator post, the tensile stress and the corresponding strain energy density become concentrated near the tips of the lateral branches, thus promoting their expansion and even causing a transverse fracture under the condition of 100 kN. In the case of a small straight compression below 25 kN, the breakdown process can be restrained. But when it comes to 75 kN, the breakdown process is promoted again, and a shear fracture can be caused above 100 kN. Under diagonal tensile or compressive stress, the breakdown channel deviates towards the applied force due to asymmetric strain energy density distribution. The objective of this research is to improve the comprehension and forecasting of breakdown in dielectric materials.

articleTitle: A lagrange-multiplier-based fast planning method for integrated community energy systems considering multiple uncertainties
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Integrated Community Energy Systems (ICES) facilitate the connection of multiple energy networks, including electricity, gas, heat, and cold networks. However, with the increasing complexity and uncertainty of loads and renewable generations, a vast number of operation scenarios must be considered for ICES planning. Although a few representative scenarios are often selected to reduce the computational burden, it can overlook scenarios that may have a significant impact on the ICES planning results. To address this issue, a Lagrange-multiplier-based fast planning method (LM) is proposed for ICES that considers massive operation scenarios without reduction. This method constructs a double-layer model to determine optimal planning schemes of ICES, including a planning configuration problem and massive operation optimization problems considering multiple uncertainties. The LM approach is applied to directly obtain the results of massive scenarios instead of time-consuming optimizations. Additionally, the optimality criteria are used to match the scenarios with Lagrange multipliers, which ensures the accuracy of planning schemes. The efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated by a typical ICES, and the planning results are analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal data graph modeling and exploration of application scenarios in “power grid one graph”
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: By modeling the spatiotemporal data of the power grid, it is possible to better understand its operational status, identify potential issues and risks, and take timely measures to adjust and optimize the system. Compared to the bus-branch model, the node-breaker model provides higher granularity in describing grid components and can dynamically reflect changes in equipment status, thus improving the efficiency of grid dispatching and operation. This paper proposes a spatiotemporal data modeling method based on a graph database. It elaborates on constructing graph nodes, graph ontology models, and graph entity models from grid dispatch data, describing the construction of the spatiotemporal node-breaker graph model and the transformation to the bus-branch model. Subsequently, by integrating spatiotemporal data attributes into the pre-built static grid graph model, a spatiotemporal evolving graph of the power grid is constructed. Furthermore, the concept of the “Power Grid One Graph” and its requirements in modern power systems are elucidated. Leveraging the constructed spatiotemporal node-breaker graph model and graph computing technology, the paper explores the feasibility of grid situational awareness. Finally, typical applications in an operational provincial grid are showcased, and potential scenarios of the proposed spatiotemporal graph model are discussed.

articleTitle: Hybrid AC/DC collection and HVDC transmission topology for large-scale offshore wind farms
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Conventional offshore wind integration systems use 33kV or 66kV AC cables to collect wind energy, coupled with high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission technology to deliver wind power to onshore grids. This scheme suffers from high cost for collection systems as well as offshore platforms when the capacity of offshore wind farms increases. This paper proposes a hybrid AC/DC collection and HVDC transmission concept for the large-scale offshore wind integration system. Wind farms close to the offshore converter platform are integrated using AC collection cables, while the remaining wind farms are integrated using DC collection cables. The AC and DC collection cables infeed to the offshore converter platform, which features a three-terminal hybrid AC/DC/DC hub. The system layout and operating principle of the hybrid AC/DC collection and HVDC transmission system are introduced in detail. The control strategy and parameter design of the hybrid AC/DC/DC hub are presented. And the economical evaluation comparing with conventional AC collection and HVDC transmission scheme is conducted. It is indicated that the proposed integration concept can reduce the operating power capacity and power loss of the offshore converter, enhancing the economic efficiency of the overall integration system. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed integration technology is validated in a 2000MW offshore wind power integration system by PSCAD/EMTDC simulation analysis.

articleTitle: Carbon reduction oriented regional integrated energy system optimization via cloud-edge cooperative framework
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: In the regional integrated energy system (RIES) with multi-participation of user side, supply side, and integrated energy retailer (IER), the interaction and collaboration among various participants in a multi-energy trading mode are difficult to be revealed under the conventional vertical integrated structure, which poses challenges to achieve an economical and low-carbon operation of RIES. To address this issue, a cloud-edge cooperative framework-based electricity-heat collaborative optimization strategy is proposed in this paper. The multi-energy trading considering carbon trading process is embedded within the cloud-edge coordination framework, where IER is considered as the cloud side, whereas the user side and supply side are considered as the edge side, and the success-history-based adaptive differential evolution (SHADE) algorithm is adopted to obtain the interaction strategy. The simulation demonstrates that compared to the conventional vertical integrated structure, the RIEs's carbon emissions have decreased by 2.4% and transaction costs have decreased by 3.4%.

articleTitle: Investigating the dynamic behavior of bubbles in oil during partial discharge
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The partial discharge occurring in the weak part of the insulation of a converter transformer results in the formation of a large number of bubbles in the insulating oil. The migration, deformation, and other dynamic behaviors of bubbles in the region of a strong electric field can cause them to easily accumulate into “small bridges” of impurities that can lead to the breakdown of the oil gap. The authors of this study experimentally investigate and discuss the mechanisms of migration and deformation of bubbles in oil during partial discharge under composite AC/DC voltage to clarify their dynamic behaviors. The influence of the initial position of the bubbles on their trajectory of migration and velocity as well as the morphological changes occurring in them were analyzed by using numerical simulations. The results show that the bubbles moved away from the strong electric field due to the action of the dielectrophoresis force. The interface of the bubbles was longitudinally stretched under the action of the electrostrictive force and the vertical component of the drag force, and gradually recovered to assume a spherical shape under the influence of surface tension and the horizontal component of the drag force.

articleTitle: Sharing of frequency response between asynchronously interconnected systems with renewable generation using LCC-HVDC
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Asynchronously interconnected AC systems with renewable generation are experiencing reducing level of frequency regulation capability from traditional providers, therefore in critical need to develop additional sources of frequency response. Motivated by this, this paper, from the grid-side perspective that has largely been overlooked in previous research, proposes a primary frequency response sharing strategy for Line-Commutated Converter based High Voltage Direct Current (LCC-HVDC) systems. The proposed method achieves the sharing of frequency response between asynchronously interconnected systems by adjusting the HVDC power during frequency events. It is accomplished through rectifier DC current control, while inverter DC voltage control is utilized to transmit inverter AC frequency information to the rectifier side. This enables the proposed control to respond to frequency events at both sending and receiving ends without relying on converter-to-converter communications. Furthermore, a mathematical model is developed to describe the coupled dynamics of AC frequencies between sending and receiving ends. Based on the model, a parameterization method is further proposed to achieve the desired frequency sharing performance. This ensures that an appropriate level of primary frequency response is shared without jeopardizing the frequency performance of the supporting-side AC system. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through real-time simulations.

articleTitle: A method applicable to the stability analysis of sub/super synchronous oscillations in PMSG integrated power system under large disturbances
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: This paper proposed an oscillation stability analysis method for evaluating the oscillation stability of PMSG integrated power system under large disturbances. The proposed method can depict the interaction path of dynamic energy within the system, quantitatively assess the influence of different energy interaction behaviors on the system's stability, and identify the key factors inducing oscillations. Firstly, based on the dynamic characteristics of different control modules during large disturbance, the system is divided into several subsystems, and energy model of each subsystem is constructed. Secondly, the interaction energy between different subsystems is extracted, the influence of the interaction energy on the system's stability is quantitatively calculated, and the key factors inducing oscillations are located. Finally, the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed oscillation stability analysis method are verified by hardware-in-loop tests. From the results, the system's oscillation stability can be accurately assessed by the proposed method under large disturbances, and the key factors inducing oscillations can be located. The proposed method can serve as a new universal solution for analyzing oscillation stability under large disturbance scenarios.

articleTitle: Dual-side closed-loop control of LCC-S WPT cascaded with secondary semi-active rectifier and controller parameter integrated design
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: In this paper, a dual-side indirect closed-loop control (DSICLC) strategy for the LCC-S compensated wireless power transmission system cascaded with the secondary semi-active rectifier (LCC-S-SAR WPT) is proposed. The indirect control of the secondary coil current is achieved by the closed-loop control of the primary inverter current. The closed-loop control of the charging current and voltage of the output side battery is achieved through the secondary semi-active rectifier. Based on the proposed DSICLC strategy, the LCC-S-SAR WPT essentially becomes a two current-source converters cascaded system. The cascade system stability cannot be ensured by the controller parameters designed according to the subsystem stability. An integrated design method of the dual-side controllers is proposed with the global stability of the current-source cascade system as a constraint. By the experiment verification, the proposed DSICLC strategy and the integrated design method of the controllers are feasible and practical.

articleTitle: Coordinated optimizing planning for AC-DC distribution networks with quantitative energy storage and converter lifetime assessment
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed power sources in distribution networks has raised concerns about power consumption. Configuring energy storage (ES) devices becomes an effective planning strategy for enhancing the consumption of distributed photovoltaics. However, ES can only cooperate with limited consumption owing to site factors and capacity constraints. This paper presents a coordinated planning scheme for distribution networks, utilizing ES to balance time-scale fluctuations and constructing medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) lines between regions to mitigate spatial-scale fluctuations. Further, in such a coordinated distribution network planning problem, the equivalent annual cost model is commonly used for estimating the lifetime of ES devices and converters, but it exhibits limitations, particularly in the neglect of charge-discharge cycles and thermal cycling of devices. To address these issues, an equipment lifetime assessment model is established for planning the optimal number, capacity, and sites of ES devices and converters. Moreover, the coordinated optimal planning problem considering equipment lifetime to minimize the total cost is formulated. Various linearization methods are applied to transform the nonconvex nonlinear problem into a mixed-integer second-order cone programming problem. Finally, the case study demonstrates the effectiveness and economy of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Optimized Temporary Frequency Support for Wind Power Plants Considering Expanded Operational Region of Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Wind power plants (WPPs) are increasingly mandated to provide temporary frequency support to power systems during contingencies involving significant power shortages. However, the frequency support capabilities of WPPs under derated operations remain insufficiently investigated, highlighting the potential for further improvement of the frequency nadir. This paper proposes a bi-level optimized temporary frequency support (OTFS) strategy for a WPP. The implementation of the OTFS strategy is collaboratively accomplished by individual wind turbine (WT) controllers and the central WPP controller. First, to exploit the frequency support capability of WTs, the stable operational region of WTs is expanded by developing a novel dynamic power control approach in WT controllers. This approach synergizes the WTs' temporary frequency support with the secondary frequency control of synchronous generators, enabling WTs to release more kinetic energy without causing a secondary frequency drop. Second, a model predictive control strategy is developed for the WPP controller. This strategy ensures that multiple WTs operating within the expanded stable region are coordinated to minimize the magnitude of the frequency drop through efficient kinetic energy utilization. Finally, comprehensive case studies are conducted on a real-time simulation platform to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

Author Keywords: Active power control model predictive control

articleTitle: Quantifying the power flexibility of a multisource looped district heating system using a region-based method
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Multisource looped district heating systems (MSL-DHSs) have the potential to provide power flexibility to electric power systems (EPSs) through coupling units. An MSL-DHS has multiple coupling units, unlike a single-source DHS. Through the coordination of coupling units and heating networks, the thermal supply sides of these units can compensate for each other, leading to numerous combinations for providing flexibility. Quantifying the flexibility of an MSL-DHS requires characterizing the intercoupling feature of multiple units and addressing the nonlinear hydraulic model. In this context, this paper proposes a power flexibility region (PFR) method to quantify the power flexibility of an MSL-DHS. The feasible region of an MSL-DHS model is projected onto the variable space of power output/input of the coupling units to construct the PFR model. A nonconvex nonlinear programming (NLP) boundary point searching model is established to calculate the PFR. To improve the computational efficiency and ensure the convergence of the boundary point searching model, a global optimization algorithm based on the reformulated piecewise McCormick envelope is proposed. Case studies are carried out on a modified 32-node MSL-DHS from Barry Island to verify the proposed method. Impacts of supply temperature, mass flow direction and heat load level on power flexibility are analyzed.

articleTitle: A faulted feeder selection method based on active harmonic injection of CIDGs for small current grounding system
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: When a single-line grounding (SLG) fault occurs in a small current grounding system (SCGS), the weak fault characteristics pose a challenge to the fault line selection (FFS). To improve the reliability of FFS, a new FFS method based on harmonic active injection of converter interfaced distributed generator (CIDG) is proposed in the paper. Firstly, by analyzing the distribution law and attenuation characteristics of the harmonic current actively injected by CIDG in the system, the active injection characteristic harmonic current signal that can meet the needs of FFS is selected, and based on this, a characteristic harmonic current signal injection method based on CIDG active control is designed. On this basis, an FFS method based on the amplitude phase relationship of harmonic current is proposed, which enables the proposed method to simultaneously meet the requirements of fault line selection and phase selection. PSCAD/EMTDC simulation analysis verified the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Multi-damping frequency-constrained unit commitment and multi-reserve resource allocation for RES-penetrated power systems
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The rapid influx of renewable energy sources (RESs) brings about significant impacts on the frequency dynamics and operational scheduling of power systems. RESs can provide rapid frequency support utilizing virtual inertia emulation or droop control. Nevertheless, the extensive integration of renewable energy generation amplifies the variability of crucial parameters in frequency control, leading to potential underdamped, overdamped, and critically damped states in the system frequency response model, thus affecting the performance of post-contingency frequency dynamics. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-damping state frequency response model. On the other hand, uncertainty surrounding renewable generation significantly impacts frequency security and system scheduling operations. This necessitates a more meticulous consideration of unit commitment (UC) and primary frequency reserves. To improve operational economics while stabilizing system frequency, the variable virtual inertia and droop factors of RESs are optimized for coordination with SGs. To this end, A robust frequency-constrained UC and multi-reserve resource allocation model is proposed. Simulation results validate the accuracy of the frequency response formula under multiple damping states, and comparative case studies demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed model.

Author Keywords: variable virtual inertia and droop factors

articleTitle: Review of nondestructive testing methods for defects in insulating polymers
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: In the field of power systems, insulating polymers have found extensive application due to their outstanding properties. However, these materials are susceptible to defects arising from various factors during production and operation, which may progress and potentially lead to safety incidents. This paper provides a comprehensive review of non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques for insulating polymers. Based on the physical principles underlying these methods, they are categorized into electrical testing methods, non-electrical passive testing methods, and non-electrical active testing methods. The paper offers a retrospective assessment of the applications of these methods in insulating polymers. Finally, a comparative analysis of the applicability, advantages, and disadvantages of these various techniques is presented, aiming to facilitate the targeted selection of the optimal NDT method in engineering applications.

articleTitle: System strength forecasting using hedge feedforward feedback-based gated recurrent unit algorithm with drift detection analysis
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: System strength or fault level forecasting knowledge has become essential for grid system operators due to the higher-penetration of renewable energy sources. To address this issue, system strength forecasting is proposed in this paper using a hedge feedforward feedback (HFF)-based online gated recurrent unit (GRU) learning algorithm. A novel framework is developed, comprised of a HFF mechanism, online deep learning processes and data drift detection approaches in order to update capacity of conventional GRU models and to enhance forecasting accuracy. Different kinds of experimental and simulated data, collected from a laboratory building management system and IEEE 39 bus test-bed system respectively, are applied to derive the relationship between system strength input level and forecasting output. The obtained results present that the designed model shows higher forecasting accuracy, even in online data screaming conditions, when compared with widely used offline learning algorithms, such as transformer and long short-term memory networks.

articleTitle: A series-connected mixed switching frequency power cells based islanded microgrid with enhanced power quality control
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: In this paper, an islanded microgrid is developed using series-connected mixed switching frequency power cells. The system consists of a few low switching frequency (LSF) power cells in a simple fixed modulation index operation manner, to reduce the switching loss and the computational load of the control system. The reference voltages of LSF power cells are obtained from a frequency inverse power factor droop controller to obtain proper power sharing between power cells without any communications. Meanwhile, there is a high switching frequency (HSF) power cell with a floating dc bus that can effectively absorb the harmonics from these LSF power cells. The HSF power cell also behaves as an inherent harmonic virtual impedance to mitigate the resonance of the islanded microgrid and to provide an accurate point of common coupling (PCC) voltage magnitude restoration. With the help of this HSF power cell, various types of power quality issues of the cascaded power cells based islanded microgrid can be solved without any interference with the power sharing among LSF power cells.

articleTitle: Cascaded modular single-stage solid-state transformer with reduced count of components
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Isolated AC/AC cascaded multilevel topologies have widespread applications across various domains, including solid-state transformer (SST), wind generator systems, and microgrids. This paper proposes a novel cascaded modular AC/AC topology based on a single-stage isolated module. The proposed converter provides direct AC/AC power conversion without four-quadrant switches, and unfolding bridges, thereby reducing the number of components, and enhancing the efficiency. The converter has a symmetrical configuration enabling seamless control of the bidirectional power flow. Moreover, the topology is electrolytic capacitorless, which enhances the power density and reduces the initial inrush currents. The isolation transformer handles high-frequency carrier components with a double line-frequency envelope, which reduces the root mean square values. The converter has zero voltage switching (ZVS) turn-on features without any auxiliary circuits or resonance. The converter modulation strategy has a straightforward switching algorithm with lower sideband harmonics than the classical methods, thereby improving the total harmonic distortion. Furthermore, a control scheme is proposed based on a phase-shift control method to regulate the load power and balance the voltage among the modules. A detailed controller design with a closed-loop transient analysis is presented. The operation principles, modulation, modeling, and ZVS analysis of the proposed topology are demonstrated. The theoretical analysis and performance of the proposed converter are validated by 1 kW experimental results.

articleTitle: Study on electric field and flashover characteristics of the roof insulators in non-uniform pollution conditions
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Influenced by high-speed airflow, pollution on the roof insulators is extremely distributed unevenly. When encountering the wet weather, the pollution will become humid and the dry bands are prone to be formed in where the leakage current is large. That makes the insulator's electric field seriously distortion and reduces its insulation performance, thus resulting to the roof insulator flashover and affecting the safe operation of the train. For this purpose, roof insulators' potential and electric field under non-uniform pollution conditions are simulated and analyzed in this paper. Then, based on leakage current distribution on pollution layer surface, the effects of dry band position, width and number on electric field of the roof insulator are researched. Ultimately, flashover tests are carried out with 3D printed insulators under high-speed airflow to examine the influence law of dry bands formation to roof insulator flashover voltage. The study can propose a technical guide for the arc suppression and structure optimization of roof insulators under high-speed airflow.

articleTitle: Efficient and stable learning for distribution network operation: A model-based reinforcement learning approach
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: This paper discusses the application of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to the economic operation of power distribution networks, a complex system involving numerous flexible resources. Despite the control flexibility improved, traditional prediction-plus-optimization models struggle to adapt to rapidly shifting demands. Modern Artificial intelligence (AI) methods, particularly DRL methods, promise faster decision-making but face challenges including inefficient training and real-world application. This study introduces a reward evaluation system to assess the effectiveness of various strategies and proposes an enhanced algorithm based on the Model-Based DRL approach. Incorporating a state transition model, the proposed algorithm augments data and enhances dynamic deduction, improving training efficiency. The effectiveness is demonstrated in various operational scenarios, showing notable enhancements in rationality and transfer generalization.

articleTitle: Novel Multi-Station Integrated System and Coordinated Control Strategy
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Current large-scale access to distributed power and rapid growth of electric vehicles are seriously affecting power quality and reliability of distribution networks. The above issues can be resolved by using a multi-station integrated system (MSIS) composed of an energy storage system, distributed generation (DG) system and transformer substation. This paper proposes a new topology and coordinated control strategy for MSIS. The top control layer receives dispatching commands from the power grid superior to realize top layer control. The soft normally open point (SNOP) receives instructions from the top control layer to realize high-degree-of-integration mode of generation-network-load-storage. Remaining converters and energy storage devices receive instructions to realize access and integration of distributed power stations, such as energy storage systems, electric-vehicle charging systems, and photovoltaic (PV) power systems. Eight working schemes of the autonomous operation of the system are analyzed. The small-signal model of the MSIS is derived. Feasibility of the proposed topological structure and control strategy for achieving a hierarchical power supply of MSIS can be verified by real-time digital simulation results.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of active distribution networks through backstepping sliding mode excitation control in hybrid drive wind farms
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Proven to exhibit high transmission efficiency, a grid-friendly topology, and notable reliability, hybrid drive wind turbines (WTs) hold significant potential to be integrated into active distribution networks (ADNs) more friendly, providing a promising alternative solution for challenges on Volt/Var controls (VVCs). Aiming at improving the voltage stability and operating flexibility of ADNs, this paper presents an advanced excitation control strategy for coordinately adjusting the output voltage and power of hybrid drive wind farms. Specifically, an improved backstepping sliding mode controller (SMC), augmented with a dedicated extended state observer (ESO), is proposed for precise regulation of the electrically-excited synchronous generators (SGs) in hybrid drive WTs. Moreover, the designed control method, with global robustness guaranteed by an exponential convergence law, can effectively handle both the parametric uncertainties and external disturbances, particularly the unexpected wake effect and coupling impacts among different WT units, without violating any constraints during transient periods. A dedicated simulation of a 1.5 MW hybrid drive WT is constructed and then verified using the developed experimental platform. Based on this, a hybrid drive wind farm model is also established for comparative case studies. Results demonstrate that the proposed approaches can effectively improve the on-grid performance of wind farms under wake effect and grid faults, ensuring power quality and supply reliability, and thereby maintaining the voltage stability of ADNs.

articleTitle: Multi-Time-Step Rolling Optimization Strategy for Post-Disaster Emergency Recovery in Distribution System Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Aimed at improving the resilience of distribution systems and analyzing the influence of uncertainties on the post-disaster emergency recovery process of a power-transportation system, this paper proposes a multi -time-step rolling optimization strategy based on model predictive control (MPC). First, the prediction models for three types of uncertainties: recovery time of faulty equipment, load demand and photovoltaic output are established. When it is assumed that traffic flow and density can meet a specific relationship, the cell transmission model (CTM) can be used to establish the transportation network. The evidence theory is used to model and analyze the two types of uncertain factors that constitute fault recovery time: travel time and repair time. Second, a mixed integer linear programming model of emergency recovery is established, in order to minimize load reduction and restoration resource scheduling cost. Decision variables include repair sequence of faulty equipment and the scheduling plan for restoration resources. Through the rolling optimization and feedback correction process, load demand can track the expected value and economic loss of power outages can be reduced as much as possible. Finally, a case study is used to verify the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper and validate a multi-time-step rolling optimization strategy has the advantages of updating uncertain information multiple times, which can achieve the goal of planning a shorter path for the repair crew and shortening the total duration of fault recovery.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Robust-Game Electricity Transaction Model for a Multi-Microgrid System Considering Wind Power Uncertainty
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Considering the uncertainty of wind power generation (WPG) and the specific operation behaviors of trading microgrids, this paper presents a blockchain-enabled robust-game electricity transaction model in a multi-microgrid system (MMS) to obtain optimal bidding-dispatching strategies, and achieve a transparent and decentralized electricity transaction. Combining blockchain technology and a non-cooperative game model, the established MMS electricity transaction architecture provides a complete information game environment for all game microgrids and facilitates the transparent, efficient, orderly, spontaneous management of MMS electricity transactions without the intervention of a third trusted party. Based on the distributed transaction architecture, an MMS robust-game model is presented to achieve the optimal day-ahead bidding-dispatching (DA-BD) strategies, in which the individual microgrid two-stage adjustable robust-game bidding-dispatching (ARG-BD) model characterizes the WPG uncertainty by employing uncertain interval and adjustable robust parameters. The binary expansion method, duality theory, big M method, and column-and-constrain generation algorithm (C&CG) are employed to solve the individual microgrid two-stage ARG-BD model. An alternating robust-game procedure integrating the C&CG algorithm and non-cooperative game model is developed to solve the MMS robust-game model. Case studies demonstrate the transparent and decentralized transaction, economic mutual benefits, and solution robustness of the presented method.

articleTitle: Integrated multiport flexible voltage clamp circuit breaker with DC chopper applied to MMC-HVDC system
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Given the wide application of DC grids, the relevant protection equipment of power grids must be improved during the fault period. This study proposes an integrated multiport flexible voltage clamp circuit breaker with a DC chopper acting on the receiving end converter to solve the DC short circuit fault and surplus power because of AC low-voltage fault; it has a modular design. As a DC circuit breaker, the device utilizes the voltage-clamping principle and thyristor semi control to remove faults. As the fault current increases, the branch circuit outputs different levels of voltage by selecting different gears, thereby controlling the voltage-clamping effect. This device can distinguish between different fault types to prevent secondary shocks in the system. As a DC chopper, the voltage at both ends of the energy dissipation resistor is varied by switching submodules, consuming surplus power in the system to complete AC low-voltage fault through and minimizing the impact of low-voltage faults on the system's transmission capacity. Finally, the effectiveness and applicability of the equipment were verified using wind turbines connected to a flexible DC transmission three-terminal power grid model in PSCAD/EMTDC, and two fault simulation types were analyzed. A comparison of the electrical quantities (fault current, system voltage and branch voltage) of the proposed circuit breaker with other similar equipment showed that due to the efficiency of the proposed equipment, the peak fault current was reduced by at least 35.8% and the required voltage stress of key power electronic equipment was reduced by at least 71.5%. Therefore, the equipment ensures that the per-unit voltage of the DC system does not exceed 1.05 during AC fault crossing.

articleTitle: Fast calculation method for the transient voltage trajectories of a hybrid AC/DC transmission system integrated with large-scale renewable energy
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy, active-reactive power coupling operation of HVDC systems and smaller number of traditional generators have increased the vulnerability of hybrid AC/DC transmission systems to various transient voltage issues. Transient voltage trajectories are crucial for precisely analyzing and controlling systems comprising heterogeneous devices under various operating and fault conditions. However, obtaining voltage trajectories typically requires time-consuming simulations of full-representation system models. Instead, a fast calculation method is proposed in this paper. First, the possible transient voltage problems are summarized through an abstracted four-machine two-area system based on the structural characteristics of actual hybrid AC/DC sending projects in China. Then, generalized formulations are proposed to describe the accurate fault ride-through characteristics of renewable energy generators, including wind turbines and PV units, considering complex interactions with the system. Based on the equivalent circuit model of the abstracted system, a fast calculation method for transient voltage trajectories is proposed based on network transformations and the improved Euler method. Compared with detailed model-based simulations, the proposed method achieves over 98% accuracy across various fault scenarios and requires only a quarter of the time consumption. When applied to large power grids, it can also achieve over 95% accuracy while consuming only one-third of the time.

articleTitle: Transient stability analysis and improvement of isolated renewable energy bases with VSC-DC transmission
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: This paper conducts research on the transient stability analysis and improvement of isolated renewable energy bases with VSC-DC transmission. First, the transient stability of the system is decomposed into two subissues: the transient stability focusing on the dynamics of grid following (GFL) and grid forming (GFM) generators inside the base, as well as the transient stability concerning the interaction between the base and the VSC-DC station. Second, these two subissues are analyzed separately, showing that the switching of GFM generators between the current source state and the voltage source state may have a negative effect on the transient stability. Finally, an adaptive voltage booster suitable for GFM generators is proposed, which is proved through a case study to be beneficial for the transient stability in discussed scenes.

articleTitle: Coordinated planning of interconnected multi-regional power systems considering large-scale energy storage system, transmission expansion, and carbon emission quota trading
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Global warming has motivated the world's major countries to actively develop technologies and make policies to promote carbon emission reduction. Focusing on interconnected multi-regional power systems, this paper proposes a coordinated planning model for interconnected power systems considering energy storage system planning and transmission expansion. A market-based carbon emission quota trading market that helps reduce carbon emissions is built and integrated into the coordi-nated planning model, where entities can purchase extra or sell surplus carbon emission quotas. Its effects on promoting carbon emission reduction are analyzed. Considering the limitations on information exchange between interconnected regional power systems, the proposed model is decoupled and solved with the analytical target cascading algorithm. A modified two-region 48-bus system is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model and solving method.

articleTitle: A cascaded multi-port converter with energy storage units for large-scale photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) power into the grid by inverting after DC boosting has become the main method for large-scale PV power plants. However, increasing the capacity, efficiency, and conversion ratios of grid-connected PV converters present major challenges. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a new converter topology consisting of an arm multiplexing multiport inverter (AMMI), an input-paralleled and out-isolated (IPOI) DC-DC converter, and distributed energy storage units (ESU). In this proposed topology, The AMMI improves sub-module utilization from 50% to 66.7%, while the medium-frequency DC/DC converter isolates and steps up the voltage, and the ESU balance the power flow of the system. The proposed converter can transmit PV power to the grid in two ways. Moreover, the control scheme of the converter is proposed in detail. Based on the simulation results, it is evident that the converter performs well in both steady-state and transient conditions.

articleTitle: Design Considerations on Voltage and Current Transfer Ratio of High-Frequency Transformers
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: A high frequency (HF) transformer is key equipment for dc-dc converter to achieve galvanic isolation and voltage transformation. As operating frequency increases, voltage and current transfer ratio of HF transformer may significantly deviate from the turn ratio due to parasitic effects, failing to transfer expected voltage and current from the primary side to the secondary side. In this paper, design considerations on voltage and current transfer ratio of the HF transformer are investigated to obtain expected transfer performance. By revealing parasitic effects on transfer characteristic (TC) of the HF transformer with load, deviation between voltage/current transfer ratio and turn ratio is correlated with the ratio of voltage/current TC resonant frequency and operating frequency. Accordingly, constraints for parasitic parameters to obtain expected transfer ratio are proposed, and practical measures to achieve improvements in transformer design are discussed. A 20kHz HF transformer prototype is used as an application, by which evaluations on deviation of voltage/current transfer ratio and turn ratio are verified, and voltage/current transfer performance of the prototype are effectively improved by optimal design based on the proposed principles.

articleTitle: Forecasting multi-timescale demand response potential using characteristic maps
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: With the increasing penetration of variable renewable energy, flexible resources are highly needed to hedge the increasing uncertainty and variability in the power system. Demand response has been serving as a cost-effective type of flexible resource in recent years. In order to balance the uncertainty of the system, it is crucial to assess how much flexibility demand response programs can provide. Thus, the forecast of demand response potential is important for the operation of the bulk system. This paper proposes a modeling approach that can characterize the multi-timescale flexibility of demand response so that not only the power potential but also temporal-coupling characteristics can be considered. Furthermore, a day-ahead demand response potential forecast method is proposed using deep convolutional generative adversarial networks. The proposed forecast method is tested using data from 170 users in Pecan Street Dataport. The result shows that the proposed method can forecast the multi-timescale flexibility of demand response with high accuracy.

articleTitle: A data-driven robust state estimation method for integrated electricity-heat system
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The integrated electricity-heat system (IEHS) has received more and more attention in recent years for its potential of improving energy utilization efficiency and hosting capacity of renewable energy. To enhance the monitoring and control of IEHS, several model-driven state estimation (MDSE) methods for IEHS have been proposed for filtering raw measurement data, improving system visibility, and helping validate the model. However, these MDSE methods are highly dependent on the accurate physical model, making them ineffective without the knowledge of the current physical model, which often occurs in practice. To this end, this paper proposes a data-driven state estimation (DDSE) method for IEHS, which constitutes an off-line learning stage and an on-line application stage. During the off-line learning stage, the partial least absolute deviation algorithm is used to suppress the collinearity and possible gross errors in the historical/simulation samples of IEHS and obtain the constant mapping matrix. During the on-line application stage, we propose a method independent of topology information to identify and replace the bad data in the present measurement snapshot using the historical/simulation data, then the state variables of the present snapshot can be rapidly and accurately obtained by matrix multiplication. We further propose a support vector classification (SVC)-based topology classification method, which makes the proposed DDSE widely applicable to different topologies. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DDSE method while ensuring high robustness and estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Scalable contract design for virtual power plant with numerous distributed energy resources considering electricity-carbon-green certificate multiple market trading
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) is a promising way to facilitate distributed energy resources (DERs) to participate in energy trading. As the actual preference of the DERs is hard to obtain, information asymmetry is a prevailing issue, which is canonically tackled by contract theory. However, the number of DERs within a VPP is generally huge, making the contract design an intractable large nonconvex program. Hence, a contract design model is established for VPP in electricity, green certificates and carbon emission rights market trading under information asymmetry, where the synergy among multiple markets is expected to contribute to a sustainable society. Then, a model reduction technique is proposed to reduce the number of nonconvex constraints in the model from OA<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) to O(V), whose exactness is strictly proved. Finally, an iterative convexification procedure is introduced to transform the nonconvex contract design problem into a series of convex programs, which can be readily handled by off-the-shelf solvers. Case studies verity both the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analysis of a lightweight 3D symmetric core for de-icer convertor transformers: No-load characteristics
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The convertor transformer is the core component of the overhead line de-icers. The high current and capacity required to melt ice results in its enormous size and weight. The three-phase 3D symmetric core has a compact structure making it lightweight. However, the current reports are not sufficient to support practical applications. To analyze the no-load characteristics of this structure, a typical transformer model was established. The magnetic flux varying law was derived. Finite Element Method (FEM) was used to simulate no-load operation and to compare it with a planar core. The effect of manufacturing-induced air gaps and the limitations of loss simulation were presented. Then, a sample transformer with a capacity of 4.0 MVA was manufactured and tested. The results show that the proposed core has the advantage of lightweight and magnetic symmetry compared to the planar core. The average error of the no-load parameters is 4.81%. Without considering the air gaps, the errors in the measured and calculated results for the no-load current and the core loss are 51.06% and 118.16%, respectively, indicating the presence of the gap effects and the simulation limitations. The accuracy of the additional loss analysis is verified via infrared thermograms. This research can support the lightweight design of convertor transformers, and reduce the cost of manufacturing and transportation of de-icers.

articleTitle: Single cable layout boundary of offshore wind turbines considering terminal voltage distribution
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: With the expansion of offshore wind farms(OWF), attention has been paid to the voltage stability of wind turbines (WT) in the scenario of island operation mode. The excessive terminal voltage of few WTs caused by the terminal voltage distribution will reduce their power generation efficiency or potentially lead to trip-off. A calculation methodology of OWFs' single cable layout boundary is proposed in this paper to optimize the number of WTs connected to a single cable. The single cable layout boundary can be used to improve the WTs' terminal voltage stability and avoid the degradation of power generation efficiency. First, the terminal voltage function is constructed based on the power flow of the π-type cable, and the terminal voltage distribution law within WTs connected to the single cable is revealed. Second, in several grid-connection voltage scenarios, the terminal voltage boundaries are calculated to restrict the number of WTs connected to the single cable. Case studies built in MATLAB are carried out for performance verification of the proposed terminal voltage boundaries. OWFs' single cable layout boundary can effectively evaluate the terminal voltage stability of WTs in current OWFs and guide the layout planning of upcoming wind farms.

articleTitle: Exploring the potential of IoT-blockchain integration technology for energy community trading: Opportunities, benefits, and challenges
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: The integration of blockchain technology with energy community trading represents a promising frontier in the energy sector, offering innovative solutions to challenges in energy trading and management. This review conducts a systematic investigation of the potential benefits, applications and challenges of blockchain in facilitating multi-level energy trading for energy communities. Firstly, the background information of the blockchain and Internet of Things (IoT) is provided, along with an elucidation of their integration architecture for energy communities. Building on this foundation, the applications of blockchain in transactive energy communities are analyzed from three perspectives: community-level energy trading, regional-level energy trading, and grid-level energy trading. Following that, the currently known projects and pilots on blockchain-based trans active energy are comprehensively summarized. Finally, key challenges in implementing blockchain-based energy trading for local energy communities are discussed, providing guidance for future research.

articleTitle: Mean-variance trading portfolio selection for a class of energy retailers
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Due to the volatile price of various energy products, energy retailers in many countries are facing the risk of going bankrupt. This paper focuses on a class of energy retailers that trade energy products including the electricity option, the natural gas option and the white certificate. From the perspective of such energy retailers, this paper studies a portfolio selection strategy that can achieve the maximized asset value and mitigate the potential risk of purchasing energy products at high prices. Firstly, a class of linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are used to model the dynamic time-varying price of electricity option, natural gas option and white certificate accurately. Secondly, based on the mean-variance model, the portfolio selection strategy problem of energy retailers trading these three products is formulated as a stochastic optimal control problem. Then, the linear-quadratic (LQ) control method is used to solve the problem analytically with mathematical theorem, and the obtain controller is indeed the desired optimal trading strategy. Finally, a series of examples demonstrating the correctness of the proposed portfolio selection strategy are provided.

articleTitle: Resilience-promoting decentralized robust synthetic restoration strategy for regional integrated energy system
publicationTitle: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems
abstract: Previous studies focused on meeting the demand of traditional single-energy loads by dispatching resources within a regional integrated energy system (RIES), ignoring the trend of multi-energy loads becoming the dominant load type. Meanwhile, uncertainty and communication link failures caused by contingencies are gradually gaining attention. Therefore, we propose a decentralized robust synthetic restoration strategy (SRS) that combines the integrated demand response (IDR) program and repair order to enhance the resilience of RIES. Considering the uncertainty of the repair time of the faulty components, we formulate the problem as a two-stage robust optimization model to minimize the restoration cost and interruption duration. To alleviate the communication tension, we propose a decentralized approach to decouple the model based on different stakeholders. Meanwhile, we develop a specific solution procedure considering the interference of binary variables and potential communication link failures on the decentralized solution.
